newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian rubber prices were stable in late trading on Thursday amid thin buying interest, traders said.
One trader said buyers bid the benchmark SIR20 for June shipment at 46.50 U.S. cents/lb fob Singapore, but traders refused to sell. Offer prices were otherwise stable despite the absence of buyers.

"It's crazy...prices keep going down. Traders are trying to attract buyers but no one is interested," said one trader. "This reminds me of 1994 when offer prices fell to as a low as 30.00 U.S. cents/lb because of poor demand," he added.
Traders said offer prices were stable at 45.75 fob Palembang, at 46.25 fob Medan, at 46.00 fob Padang and Surabaya and at 45.75 fob Pontianak and Jambi.
Traders have reported some inquiries for August/September shipment but they refused to sell because prices were too low.
